mcqs.question: You need to run your primary database with automatic failover. Should you use an edge location for the standby replica?
options: Yes, edge locations are the fastest option available
It doesn't matter, all provider locations offer the same capabilities
Yes, as long as the edge location is in the same country
No — edge locations are for caching/serving content close to users, not for running databases
mcqs.explanation: Edge locations are lightweight points of presence for caching and content delivery — they don't host full compute or databases. A database standby belongs in another Availability Zone (or region), not an edge location.

mcqs.question: Your app server makes a chatty, latency-sensitive call to a cache on every request. Where should the cache live relative to the app server?
options: In the same AZ, or at least the same region, to minimize round-trip latency
In a different region, for maximum durability
It doesn't matter — cross-region latency is negligible for caches
In an edge location, since caches always belong at the edge
mcqs.explanation: Chatty, latency-sensitive calls should stay as close as possible — same AZ or same region — since cross-region latency (tens to 100+ ms) would dominate request time. Cross-region placement is for durability against region-wide failure, not for this kind of hot-path traffic.

mcqs.question: In a 3-tier app spread across two AZs, why does the database tier need special handling beyond simply running two instances?
options: Databases don't support running across AZs at all
The database needs a designated primary and standby with replication, not two independent stateless copies like the web tier
It doesn't — treat it exactly like the stateless web tier
Databases should only ever run in a single AZ for consistency
mcqs.explanation: Unlike stateless web/app instances that can run identically in parallel, a database needs one authoritative primary with a replicating standby so data stays consistent and failover doesn't lose writes — a fundamentally different pattern from the stateless tiers.
